lessons: Brief workers: no expect/unwrap in production paths, even on infallible-by-construction values; the code reviewer fails it (b3fcd297 R1).

cargo-ci exits 75 (infra) when host load1 >= 0.17 x CPUs (4.08 here); many parallel worker builds trigger it. gate.sh now waits for load < 3.8 while holding the exclusive lock, and retries on exit 75.
Never pipe a check into tail before committing (b3fcd297/c400730c merge): the pipe masks the exit status. A conflict merge committed a missing brace; a fix commit followed.
Landing on drift must hold the exclusive CI lock across merge-main, cargo-ci and the main merge; otherwise other leads' merges cause endless re-gates (c400730c needed 4 cargo-ci runs).

Never rewrite a lead script in place while a background run uses it (bash reads scripts incrementally): write a new file and mv it over, so running shells keep the old inode. 6e8b9f31's ship broke this way.
Verify a task id by title before citing it in a brief (98404e0c R1 failed on a lead-supplied wrong id).
Preserve authored optional keys in typed rule configs (Option + one accessor) so serialization emits the same keys (af9c277d decision).

Briefs must not exempt sites a criterion covers: e1a6c8c2 REQ-01 covers well-known directories, so '.jit/issues' literals are in scope even though issue_record() comes later. Also: brief Codex to run cargo test -p jit-server whenever loaders the server uses change.
Code-review applies 'no literal in the listed files' to test modules too; brief file-scoped literal criteria as whole-file.
A Claude worker can stall when the auto-mode classifier errors on every tool call; preserve its WIP with a lead-preserve commit and continue on Codex.

Do not exclude a site from a task because a sibling owns its type: 91081bd3's brief exempted archive/document scopes (c1c86312), and code-review failed REQ-01 on them. Split by what each criterion names, not by enum ownership.
An alias-flip cargo check stops at lib errors and never type-checks cfg(test); grep the changed API's call sites and comparisons in all test modules too (f265e748, 3 review rounds).
Unresolved request text is not an IssueId; error/DTO carriers of it stay strings (8acca4f4).
Codex re-adds #[allow(...)] even when a rework item forbids it; grep the diff for #[allow before review.
Write story-review gap tasks as class sweeps over the whole crate, not single sites (83d04069 needed 3 rounds).
The cargo-ci suite budget can fail on a quiet start when load rises mid-run (63 s vs 11.5 s alone); confirm with a nextest timing run before treating it as a regression.
Run cargo-ci on the branch before code-review; review fails unverified backend/test criteria otherwise.
State dev/active/ out of footprint in Codex briefs; workers rewrite other epics planning docs in prose sweeps.
Code-review treats "no code path creates X" as a type-level guarantee; check staged criteria before dispatch.

First cargo-ci after a crate-source change can fail commands::{validate,profile} tests with "profiled-repository fixture ... is busy": a cold fixture build exceeds PROFILED_REPOSITORY_FIXTURE_LOCK_BOUND (12 s) under load (2a6bc44c defect, c780514e-owned, reported by 4f 2026-10-29). Re-run cargo-ci before treating it as a worker failure.

Under the alias, construction sites (raw value -> IssueId) fail REQ-03-style criteria just like uses; a generated UUID needs an infallible constructor on both sides of the bridge (IssueId::from_uuid), not a serde round-trip, which Codex tried and the lead removed.

Read land.sh output before closing: a landing cargo-ci can fail after a passing ci-only (19d9bd7d: crate_source_digest self-check mismatch from a stale shared target). cargo clean -p jit in the worktree and re-land; jit issue update --state done on unpassed gates diverts to gated.
Parallel retypes that touch one test file conflict at landing (89e7a273 vs 19d9bd7d in scope_validation_tests.rs, same retype on both sides); resolve to main and re-land.
Stored gate-run records predate format changes; test byte identity over records whose decoded key set equals the stored one, and ids over the rest.
The lead's Bash cwd must not end inside a worker worktree: the harness pins the session there. Lead state runs via env -C <root>; do not reclaim the pinned worktree while it is the cwd.
A branch's first cargo-ci after a main merge can fail crate_source_digest self-check from a stale target; cargo clean -p jit in that worktree and re-land.
cargo clean -p jit before every gated cargo-ci: merging main leaves a stale compiled-in source digest often enough to cost a gate cycle per landing.
